Current theme · the art behind the look

Abel Iloko

The handwoven textile of the Ilocos region, and why its patterns frame this app

🧵 What is Abel Iloko?

Abel is the Ilocano word for weaving, and inabel means "woven". Abel Iloko is the handwoven cloth of the Ilocos region in northern Luzon, made in Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union and Abra. It is woven from cotton thread on a wooden foot-pedal (treadle) loom, usually by women who learned the craft from their mothers and grandmothers.

The fabric is prized because it is durable, absorbent and cool in a hot climate, and it grows softer with every wash. It is used for blankets, towels, clothing, curtains, table runners and bags, and it has long been given as a gift for weddings, births and homecomings.

🎨 The patterns you see in this app

The plate list on the left and the heading bars of every plate use designs drawn from abel cloth: rows of solid and outlined diamonds, crosses and dots, and bold bands of colour. Each plate uses a different colourway, the way a weaver varies the same motif from one piece to the next.

🌀 Classic designs

  • Binakol (also binakul or binakael, from the Ilocano word for "twill"): a dizzying, interlocking pattern of geometric shapes that creates an optical illusion. By tradition it was believed to confuse and ward off wandering spirits, so it was often used for blankets that protected the sleeper.
  • Kusikos (also kusikok): a whirlwind motif within the binakol family that creates an optical illusion.
  • Sinan-sabong: flower-like designs.
  • Inuritan: geometric patterns such as diamonds and lines, the family of designs used in this theme.
  • Pinilian: a brocade technique in which extra threads are picked up by hand to raise a design on the surface of the cloth.

🏅 Keepers of the craft

Weaving towns such as Paoay and Pinili in Ilocos Norte, Vigan in Ilocos Sur and Bangar in La Union keep the tradition alive. In 2012, Magdalena Gamayo of Pinili, Ilocos Norte, was named a National Living Treasure (Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan) on 8 November 2012 for her mastery of abel weaving and for teaching it to the next generation. In 2024 the nation marked her 100th birthday with a Centennial Year in her honor.

Machine-made fabrics have made handwoven cloth rarer, and many communities now work to train young weavers, document old designs and help weavers earn a fair living from their work.

🩺 A lesson for medical students

An abel weaver builds a whole cloth one thread at a time, row after row, until a pattern appears that could never be seen from a single pass of the shuttle. Medical school works the same way. Every chapter you read, every question you answer and every case you work through is one more thread. Keep weaving: the pattern of a physician emerges over time.

Plate III · A message for the future physician

Welcome Message from the Mentor

A personal message from the mentor to every medical student
PLE REAP
Medicine
Mentor

Janill I. Magano, MD, MHPEd, DipAIML

  • Master in Health Professions Education
  • Professor III and Dean, College of Medicine, Tarlac State University
Dear Future Physician,

Medicine asks a great deal of you: long lectures, thick textbooks, early duties and examinations that never seem to end. My Med APP was made so that all of that effort turns into real understanding and strong performance, in class, in your examinations and, one day, at the bedside.

It was designed precisely for you. It follows the subjects of your year level, from Anatomy, Biochemistry and Physiology in first year to the clinical sciences of your later years. Every subject opens in Let’s Build, where concepts are explained clearly and in order, and continues in Let’s Exercise, where you test yourself until recall becomes second nature. Today tells you what to study now, what is due for review and where you are weakest, and your Tree of Life grows with every subject you complete.

Let me be clear about one thing: My Med APP does not aim to replace your textbooks and standard references. It complements them. Its work is to take information that is hard to consume and turn it into something more digestible, so that what you read in your books finally sticks. Around that content, it builds a whole universe of active recall and generation-sensitive learning experiences, where you retrieve, produce, sort, solve and explain rather than simply reread, because that is how learning becomes durable. When a topic needs more depth, go back to your books; when it needs to be remembered, come back here.

Nothing here is decoration. Each feature rests on what learning science shows works: recalling before you look at the answer, spacing your reviews over time, getting feedback right away and studying what matters most first. The mnemonics, the flashcards and the games are here because learning should also be enjoyable, and enjoyment is what keeps you coming back.

This app is the product of creativity, innovation and science, the very traits that define your generation. You think quickly, you learn in many ways at once, and you expect your tools to keep up with you. My Med APP was built to do exactly that.

Use it every day, even for a few minutes. Recall before you reveal. Review what you missed. Rest when you must, and come back the next day.

Thrive in med school. I look forward to seeing you become the physician you are meant to be.

Janill I. Magano, MD, MHPEd, DipAIMLMentor, PLE REAP Medicine2008 Ten Outstanding Students of the Philippines (Malacanang Palace)2024 Nominee for The Outstanding Young Men of the Philippines

Who we are

From one app to whole review programs

Thrive in medical school.

PLE REAP began with a plain need: medical and nursing students and graduates wanted help that was convenient, accessible and in their pocket. The answer was a mobile app, designed by professionals with extensive backgrounds in their fields, including physicians and educators who know what medical school demands.

That app has since grown into a complete study companion covering the core and clinical subjects of the medical curriculum, and into program lines that serve students, graduates and practising professionals.

Plate VII · What your examinations weigh

Valuing Content and Cognitive Demands

How much each topic is worth and how deeply each subject asks you to think, for all 12 subjects
PLE REAP
Medicine
⚖️Valuing contentWhat is worth the mostEach subject has 100 items. Its topics are ranked by their weight in the Table of Specifications, so the heaviest come first.
🧠Cognitive demandsHow deeply you must thinkEvery item sits at a level of the Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy, from Remembering to Creating. The mix tells you how to study.

🧠 The six cognitive levels, with an example of each

The Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy (Anderson and Krathwohl, 2001) sorts questions by the kind of thinking they demand. The levels build on each other: you cannot apply what you do not understand, and you cannot understand what you cannot remember. The lower three ask what you know; the upper three ask what you can do with it. Medical school examinations lean on Remembering and Understanding in the basic sciences, and on Applying, Analyzing and Evaluating in the clinical subjects. Tap a level, read how it works, then answer its sample question.

🎯 Name the level

Read each question and pick the cognitive level it tests. You do not need to answer it; only classify it.

Let’s Build · Modular Sheets

A rapid review of every subject, built for efficient study

Each subject has its own interactive review sheet, arranged topic by topic, with concise discussions, tables, interactives, must-know points and its own quiz mode.

🎯Why it is here

To help you study efficiently and remember more: see a whole subject at a glance, understand how its topics connect, master the high-yield concepts, processes and algorithms, and check yourself before lecture exams, rotations and the Board examination.

📘A rapid review, not a replacement

The sheets condense each topic into its essentials. They do not replace your textbooks, lectures and references. When you need the full discussion, go back to your books and the sources listed in the References chapter of each sheet.

🗂️Organized by Board topics

Chapters follow the topics of the Physician Licensure Examination. Most other topics taught in the medical curriculum are covered as well, placed under the chapter where they fit best.

🔍Can’t find a topic?

Use the search bar at the top of the plate list. It searches inside every Let’s Build and Let’s Exercise sheet and opens the sheet at the exact spot.

Plate XI.3 · Problem-based, simulation-based learning

Let’s Heal

One patient, twelve subjects: work a case from the barangay to the ward and back to the community
PLE REAP
Medicine

Two ways to work a case

Every patient in Let’s Heal can be worked in two modes. They use the same patient but train different things, so try both.

📚Mode 1Across the Disciplines

A guided, self-paced walk through one patient, scene by scene, from the barangay to the ward and back to the community. At each scene you complete tasks and open lenses that show how each of the 12 subjects explains what is happening, from the anatomy and pathology behind the signs to the pharmacology, ethics and public health of the plan.

  • ⏸️ No clock: pause, reread and go back
  • 🔬 Builds integration: one patient, every subject
  • 🎯 Best when you are learning or reviewing a topic
🚑Mode 2In Real World

A live simulation of the same patient on a running clock that does not pause, as on duty, played in full screen. The patient lies in a 3D bed in front of you, breathing, changing colour and moving as the case describes, and monitors, lines and oxygen appear only when you order them. The patient, relatives and staff speak to you, and you answer with numbered response cards or act from the tabs. Some choices help, some change nothing and some cause harm: every action is graded as critical, essential, neutral or wrong, and a missed critical action or a critical error costs extra points. The debrief ends with a short discussion of the condition.

  • ⏱️ Real-time pressure: delays have consequences
  • 🔁 Failed a case? Retry it before you read the debrief
  • 🩺 Builds clinical decision-making and priorities
  • 🎯 Best after you have built and exercised the topic

💡 The difference in one line: Across the Disciplines asks “Why is this happening, in every subject?”; In Real World asks “What will you do now, before time runs out?”

Plate XIV · For the mind

Self-care Podcasts

Six audio companions for worry, fear and anxiety before the examination
PLE REAP
Medicine
🎧 Put your earphones on

Take one slow breath. Then press play.

Worry, fear and anxiety are normal as the examination comes closer. They are not a sign that you are failing. These six audio guides were made for those moments. Choose the one that matches how you feel right now.

How are you feeling right now?

Tap the line that sounds most like you. The plate will point to the podcast to start with.

🌬️ One minute of breathing

No earphones nearby? Follow the circle. Breathe in for 4, hold for 4, breathe out for 6. Five rounds take about a minute.

Ready
You do not have to carry this alone. If the worry stays heavy for days, keeps you from sleeping or eating, or feels like too much, talk to someone you trust or to a mental health professional. Asking for help is part of taking care of a future doctor.
📞 If you are thinking of harming yourself, or the feeling is too heavy right now, call the NCMH Crisis Hotline. It is free, confidential and open 24 hours a day, every day.
